chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Brother Richard, barber and inventor: block signal, gearshift and torpedo
summary: Richard barbered by day and invented at night, including a railroad block signal, an automotive gearshift and a guided torpedo the government took.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: So both Tom and Richard were barbers. Is that right?
I see. Well, you mentioned that Tom had had a barber shop in San Francisco but I didn't realize that Richard also was a barber. But I...
Richard was a barber, yeah, in his spare time in a... He always had a barber shop where he... He rent a place where he got a big space in the back...
For his inventions and things. He'd barber all day and work all night on his inventions and things.
You showed me some of the blueprints for Richard's inventions but we haven't talked about Richard on the tape. Tell me on the tape now about some of the things that Richard invented.
I told you that the block signal was his first big invention--on the railroad. Then he had...oh, he had so many little things. I don't know. I'd have to look them up over there.
One was a gearshift for an automobile.

Automobile...automotive gearshift and he worked on the torpedo for the government. They had him down at Long...Santa Monica to...you know, when you have the swimming--what, do you call them? Inside swimming? Plunge, I guess you'd call...in the...in the baths where they had swimming and everything, and he had little torpedoes and boats and things in there. After they'd quit swimming and things at night, he'd...they'd allow him in there, and he'd shoot these little torpedoes and things at these boats, and he come up with this torpedo that you guide from one ship to its destination so you never miss, and when he got through with that, the government took

everything--all the wire...every wire, every screw, everything they could take, and I don't know what they paid him. You know, he was very secretive about what he got, you know, and he...uh, they took everything away, and he... Oh, he invented little things from needle-threaders on up to...
